title: `sqlparse.split` returns a whole `BEGIN TRANSACTION ... END TRANSACTION` script as one statement
spec:
This is the sqlparse library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`.

Splitting a script that wraps its work in an explicit transaction gives back a single statement instead of one per `;`.

```python
import sqlparse
sql = ("BEGIN TRANSACTION;\n"
       "DELETE FROM a WHERE id = 1;\n"
       "INSERT INTO a SELECT * FROM b;\n"
       "END TRANSACTION;")
sqlparse.split(sql)
```
Expected: `['BEGIN TRANSACTION;', 'DELETE FROM a WHERE id = 1;', 'INSERT INTO a SELECT * FROM b;', 'END TRANSACTION;']`
Actual: the whole input as a single string.

The same happens when a formatter has put the keywords on separate lines (`BEGIN\nTRANSACTION;` ... `END\nTRANSACTION;`); those should split into the same four statements, keeping the line break inside the first and last one.

`BEGIN TRANSACTION` starts a transaction, not a `BEGIN ... END` block, so the statements inside it must be split as usual. Real `BEGIN ... END` blocks in procedures and triggers must still be kept together.
acceptance: Both reported scripts split into four statements, with `BEGIN TRANSACTION;` / `END TRANSACTION;` (or their two-line forms) as the first and last
Existing BEGIN ... END block splitting is unchanged
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
